parameters.content:
# Extract invoice data with Temlavo in a reusable sub-workflow

## Who is this for?
Automation builders who receive invoice files through Gmail, Google Drive, webhooks, or other workflows and need structured accounting data with explicit review outcomes.

## What it does
This reusable sub-workflow accepts one PDF, JPEG, or PNG invoice, creates a Temlavo document, uploads the file, confirms the upload, and polls for the result. It separates completed, needs_review, failed, and recovery-stop outcomes before returning one item to the calling workflow. Review results retain extracted data and review reasons. Completed means no blocking declared check, not independently verified accounting data.

## Setup
First [register at Temlavo](https://temlavo.com/sign-up), then open [API keys](https://temlavo.com/app/api-keys) and create a key. Copy the full key shown once; the shortened key hint will not work.

Import and save this workflow in n8n. Create one HTTP Header Auth credential: Name Authorization; Value Bearer followed by one space and your full Temlavo API key. Select it on Create Document, Confirm Upload, and Get Document only.

From your existing workflow, use Execute Sub-workflow with Wait for Sub-Workflow Completion enabled. Pass binary.invoice plus the temlavo_submission object described in the input sticky note. Keep the trigger on Accept all data so the file is preserved. Process one invoice per call.

## Requirements and customization
Requires a Temlavo account, API key, available usage, and a supported invoice up to 20 MiB. The template is free; Temlavo API usage follows [Temlavo pricing](https://temlavo.com/pricing), and your n8n hosting costs are separate. Connect the returned outcome to your own accounting, notification, or review steps. See the canvas notes for retries and data retention.

nodes.name: Input — connect your Gmail, Drive, or webhook workflow

parameters.content:
## One invoice per call
Keep **Accept all data** on the trigger. In the parent, use Execute Sub-workflow, **Run once with all items**, and **Wait for Sub-Workflow Completion**. For batches, use Loop Over Items with batch size 1.

Pass one item with **binary.invoice** and this JSON:

```json
{
  "temlavo_submission": {
    "idempotency_key": "YOUR_SAVED_OPAQUE_TOKEN",
    "input_ref": "YOUR_SAVED_RETRY_RECORD_TOKEN",
    "filename": "invoice.pdf",
    "content_type": "application/pdf",
    "line_items": "advisory"
  }
}
```

Use the actual filename/MIME. Supported MIME: application/pdf, image/jpeg, image/png. Both tokens must be 1–128 letters, digits, underscores or hyphens; use UUIDs, never email addresses or invoice numbers. Save the tokens, original file, and options in your own system **before calling**. Reuse them for retries; choose new tokens only for a new logical submission. Do not generate a key inside a retry loop.

For Gmail, split attachments into individual items and map the selected attachment to binary.invoice. Ignore unrelated attachments explicitly in your parent; never pass several invoices in one call.

nodes.name: Upload — credential isolation and replay safety

parameters.content:
## Create → signed upload → confirmation
Select the same Temlavo HTTP Header Auth credential on **Create Document**, **Confirm Upload**, and **Get Document**. Leave **Signed PUT (isolated)** unauthenticated: it forwards only the API-returned upload headers.

An awaiting-upload replay confirms before sending bytes again. An ambiguous upload is also confirmed first. Retries keep the same saved submission identity.

The API origin is fixed in Validate invoice input; the caller cannot override it. Restrict who can call this sub-workflow in n8n workflow settings, because calls use your Temlavo account and allowance.

nodes.name: Outputs — completed, review, failure, or recovery

parameters.content:
## Route the returned item in your parent
**status = completed:** full document, including warnings. Continue according to your business rules.
**status = needs_review:** full document plus review_reasons. Preserve the result and send it to your review step. This is not a transport error.
**status = failed:** terminal processing failure; do not treat it as an extracted result or automatically resubmit.
**schema_version = temlavo.n8n-safe-stop.v1:** a bounded recovery stop (for example billing, rate limiting or polling timeout). Follow recovery_action using the saved input; never assume the document was cancelled.

Input validation or n8n runtime failures fail the sub-workflow. Configure the parent Execute Sub-workflow node's **On Error → Continue (using error output)** to handle these separately. Keep the normal output and error output separate.

Terminal results include input_ref for correlation; safe stops preserve their strict schema. Return to caller removes binary files and upload context.

## Operational limits
Target n8n 2.36.7. Up to 3 create attempts, 3 confirmation attempts, 20 polls; HTTP timeout 60 seconds and workflow timeout 10 minutes. A timeout does not cancel Temlavo processing. Inspect the same document or recover with the same saved submission.

line_items: **advisory** (default-style behavior), **review_on_failure**, or **required**. Required asks for minimum usable line items; it is not independent source verification.

Portable execution-history saving is disabled. n8n may still persist running/waiting execution data and binary files. Configure pruning, binary retention, backups and logs on your instance and on parent workflows before real invoices. Temlavo deletion does not delete your n8n or downstream copies. Use synthetic data for demonstrations; never pin real invoices, credentials, or responses into a shared template.
